Reported growth is strong but half of FY26 revenue is trading, manufactured growth includes repricing/bought-in fabric, and profitable years have consumed cash. Serious pending group/promoter GST allegations, related-party classification/comparability, post-IPO funding and new-listing liquidity remain unresolved. material_facts: Repeated FY23–25 RPT disclosure omissions required correction and a pending ROC adjudication application.
Hind and an issuer promoter face a material pending GST invoice-substance allegation; the related plant, trading transfer and receivable links heighten minority concerns.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: The commercial RPT disclosure correction is supported by auditor explanation. GST notices remain pending allegations; no final finding, issuer diversion or automatic issuer liability is established.
factor_audit.rationale: Repeated disclosure weakness and serious unresolved concerns support GOV 4 and G1 Hold. Sufficient adverse findings for a score of 3 or below or an evidenced gate failure are not established.

material_facts: Commodity polymer packaging and granule trading face low barriers and delayed input-cost pass-through.
Eastern distribution and installed processes support service, but 85.27% West Bengal and 40.07% top 10 customer sales constrain bargaining.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Certifications, customization, long promoter experience and lower top customer share are genuine operational strengths.
factor_audit.rationale: A useful local operating position is not evidence of durable excess economics; no moat credit for capacity alone.

material_facts: Reported three-year revenue CAGR 57.43% and 42% FY26 growth in total quantity sold show meaningful scale.
Group trading transfer, leased capacity, polymer price increases and bought-in fabric processing prevent a comparable organic-volume revenue bridge.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: FY26 sales growth is not entirely price inflation, and higher manufactured revenue is partly supported by external fabric purchases.
factor_audit.rationale: NS under actual REV rubric because no reliable comparable underlying window exists; neither a neutral score nor automatic 9 from reported CAGR. Five-year primary series and constant-perimeter decomposition are missing.

material_facts: Recurring agricultural/industrial packaging demand and proposed 4800 MT Phase IV offer an accessible regional runway.
Approvals, execution, working capital and existing geographic concentration constrain realizable growth.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Phase III trial run and high historical utilization support real customer demand, while pan India ambitions remain unproven.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed runway, distinct from CAP; total proposed capacity is not demand or profit.

material_facts: Two-year incremental post-tax operating book return 14.04% is near a 13–17% reasoned WACC range.
No attributable commissioned cohort economics; group facility transfer and bought-in fabric/repricing changed business perimeter.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: IC bridge reconciles and operating EBIT rose substantially; unverified returns are not assigned a low made-up score.
factor_audit.rationale: NS. Project sensitivity includes full capex and working capital but is not disclosure-backed proof of actual expansion returns.

material_facts: Three-year CFO/PAT−2.75 x and FCF−94.92 crore show persistently negative cash realization across profitable years.
FY26 inventory/receivable absorption and sharp >6 month AR increase overwhelm operating earnings; excluding security-deposit movement does not cure it.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Volume scaling and group plant expansion explain part of the build; most AR remains undisputed/recent and payables provide cash.
factor_audit.rationale: Persistent multi-year weakness, not a transient capex deduction; explicit GQS cap 5 applies.

material_facts: March unrestricted cash of 0.0831 crore is tiny beside 165.19 crore debt and 20.12 crore demand loans.
July debt and completed IPO improve the information set, but final net proceeds/current resources and stress drawability remain unreconciled.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: CARE 4 May adequate-liquidity opinion, historic unutilized limits and real IPO equity are substantial counterevidence; do not assert default.
factor_audit.rationale: NS and G3 Hold pending a published/current obligations/resources bridge, not a mechanical demand for private daily bank statements.

material_facts: Existing operations scaled and Phase III 1200 MT trial run occurred July 2026.
Phase IV remains proposed; CTO and remaining Phase III timing/funding descriptions need confirmation.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Reported growth and high utilization show operations are not merely planned, and third-party fabric processing adds flexibility.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed execution; no credit for 18,070 MT as commissioned or for promised April 2027 economics.

material_facts: FY26 operating EBITDA 38.04 and PAT 16.01 crore materially exceed FY25; other income is small.
Inventory gains, changing mix, taxes and post-IPO share dilution complicate persistence; current-share FY26 EPS 7.70 differs from pre-IPO 10.55.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Higher tax rate and one-time MAT effects depressed rather than flattered FY26 net margin; operating profit growth is real in reported accounts.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed earnings quality; use normalized 30% tax and ex-other-income bridge, no substitution of PAT growth for REV.

material_facts: Current funding not verified; ordinary/non-rescue return fields remain null.
Base hypothetical rescue IRR 6.20% requires financing that is not known available.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Bull rescue case ispositive but cannot be treated as ordinary expected return.
factor_audit.rationale: NS: no return-spread score from an unfinanceable or unverified ordinary scenario.

material_facts: Linked customer/margin/inventory stress creates large permanent equity loss in bear case.
Demand debt rollover and thin liquidity can force adverse financing while secured lenders have priority.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Real operations andassets, no verified default, completed IPO and positive operating earnings provide recovery support.
factor_audit.rationale: Material permanent-loss risk; not a claim a hypothetical shortfall has occurred.

material_facts: Current-share historical P/E 12.42 x does not include growth funding requirements or prove cheapness.
Base rescue return falls below 15% hurdle; stronger mix, working-capital control, rollovers and exit multiple must all hold.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: EV/EBITDA is not extreme on stale balance inputs andbull growth could deliver; uncertainty is not generic expensiveness.
factor_audit.rationale: Price-implied expectations are demanding relative to capital absorption; P is not a business-predictability score.

material_facts: Only 20 sessions since IPO and 18 secondary OHLCV prints, not a complete verified 60 session history.
Last observed volume of one 1200 share lot means zero one-lot capacity at 2/5/10% participation.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Observed medians over other print days arehigher, and the security is not declared suspended.
factor_audit.rationale: NS: secondary history, missing prints, unverified groups/queues and short seasoning prevent a canonical point.

gates.rationale: Serious pending GST allegations involve a promoter and Hind, the group plant/trading-transfer counterparty. Repeated RPT omissions add concern. The RHP records pending status, not proved misconduct. No substantiated diversion or final adverse finding is assumed.

gates.resolution: Auditor-backed counterparty/netting bridge and comparable manufacturing/trading volume, external fabric and transferred-business reconciliation.

gates.name: Funding and survival
gates.rationale: Completed IPO and July debt disclosure are positive, but final net proceeds/earmark uses, unrestricted resources, current unsecured debt and credible stressed drawing capacity are not reconciled. Diagnostic gaps are not actual default findings.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Injecto is a regional polypropylene packaging manufacturer and polymer trader, not a pure specialty-polymer compounder. Reported growth is strong but half of FY26 revenue is trading, manufactured growth includes repricing/bought-in fabric, and profitable years have consumed cash. Serious pending group/promoter GST allegations, related-party classification/comparability, post-IPO funding and new-listing liquidity remain unresolved. BQS, GQS and IAS are NS, with exact missing-factor bounds rather than invented scores. No ordinary target price or investable return is supportable at the secondary ₹ 95.70 reference.

The principal positive is an established production and customer base, completed fresh-equity IPO and partial expansion trial run. The principal risks are unresolved integrity and transaction-substance questions, inventory-led cash absorption, and the uncertain economics of additional capacity. The GST matters are pending allegations, not proved fraud or automatically issuer liabilities. Clean evidence on those matters, cash conversion and attributable returns would matter more than announced capacity.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Injecto Polymers Limited; former Injecto Polymers Private Limited. CIN U28113WB1998PLC087875. BSE SME 544930 / INJECTO; ISIN INE1JJF01019; incorporated 4 September 1998, public conversion certificate 8 July 2024. Cutoff 20 October 2026, India time; valuation reference 19 October 2026 secondary close ₹ 95.70. Current issued 20,789,600 shares gives ₹ 198.96 crore market capitalization. There is no separate NSE investment security merely because the interoperable master says INJECTO$. [E01,E16,E20]

Scope is standalone Indian GAAP under notified Accounting Standards, including AS 3, AS 18 and AS 15. The examiner’s boilerplate mentions Ind AS rules, but detailed policies and AS statements govern this analysis. Group entities are not automatically subsidiaries, and their debts/assets are not consolidated. Fiscal year ends 31 March. Model horizon is 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031; hurdle is an explicit 15% nominal pretax annualized equity return; the ₹ 5 lakh liquidity reference is illustrative, not an allocation recommendation.

G1 Hold — unresolved; G2 Hold — unresolved; G3 Hold — unresolved; G4 Hold — unresolved. High confidence in extracted primary P&L, cash-flow and specific balance lines; Medium in the short reported history and operating explanation; Low in comparable organic growth, incremental capital returns, current funding and executable liquidity. Overall investment confidence is Low because the weakest material links remain unresolved. Three complete audited/restated years are available, not a falsely completed five-year forensic series. Earlier rounded secondary figures are context only.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
BQS, Growth Quality Score (GQS) and IAS remain NS. Known factors are GOV 4, MOAT 4, DUR 5, CASH 2, EXEC 5, EARN 6, D 3 and P 3. REV, CAP, BAL, R and L are NS. Missing factors are not assigned neutral values or renormalized away. GOV 4 does not trigger the governance override; the serious unresolved allegations support G1 Hold, not an evidenced Fail. CASH 2 triggers the GQS cap of 5, but an incomplete point remains NS.

Exact Decimal weights and contributions are embedded. BQS known contribution 2.70 at 68% coverage yields bounds 3.02–5.90. GQS known contribution 2.10 at 45% coverage yields 2.65–7.60, or 2.65–5.00 after the cap. IAS known contribution 0.90 at 30% coverage yields 1.60–7.90. Bounds describe missing inputs, not probabilities or ranks. Moving GOV and MOAT each by one point changes known BQS by 0.40; moving DUR and EARN each by one changes known GQS by 0.35. No favorable classification is inferred from a partial bound. [E01–E22]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Manufacturing converts polypropylene and related inputs into woven fabrics, sacks and bags, including BOPP, lined and FIBC variants; the broad catalog also mentions leno, pouches and non-woven applications. It is not evidence of separately profitable medical, specialty-chemical or patented-material franchises. FY26 recorded ₹ 117.58 crore PP fabrics and ₹ 68.83 crore PP fabric bags; granule/PVC trading contributed ₹ 189.12 crore, or 50.36% of sales. Subtype revenue/margins are not disclosed, so product names are not fabricated segments. [E04,E05]

Unit I is the owned Jaugram facility; Unit II is the group-owned Hind Polyfabs plant under successive 11-month leave-and-license terms, with renewal arrangements up to seven years. Customer specifications feed extrusion, weaving, lamination, printing, stitching, testing and dispatch. Bought-in PP fabric procurement rose from ₹ 23.60 crore to ₹ 63.23 crore, allowing downstream processed sales to rise without equivalent own-tape tonnage. That is an economically important distinction between output, processed goods and revenue.

Customers are mainly institutional/industrial B 2 B buyers. Top 10 contribute 40.07%, largest 11.49%; West Bengal 85.27% and eastern states together 92.31%. Repeat business and food-grade quality certifications matter, but sales are purchase-order driven and do not imply take-or-pay protection. Cash must fund bulk inventory and customer credit while banks and unsecured corporate lenders provide working capital.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible mechanism is local service, product customization, established supply relationships and proximity to eastern agriculture/industry. Evidence is long operating history, actual production, a diversified bag catalog and recurring institutional customers. Durability is contestable: standard woven packaging and resin trading have replicable technology, fragmented competition, raw-material availability and weak pricing freedom. Failure can come through price competition, customer switching, higher freight into new markets or loss of leased Unit II. [E05,E06,E15,E21]

Supplier top 10 account for 72.72% of procurement, increasing dependency, while largest customer share declined from 18.91% to 11.49%, a real improvement. No verified market-share denominator establishes leadership. Certifications qualify products but do not by themselves establish excess returns. Raw material is petrochemical-linked; contracts do not establish immediate automatic cost pass-through. CARE’s May 2026 comments attributed inventory gains to earlier low-cost purchases and discussed delayed recovery of input-price shocks. These are dated rating observations, not a permanent margin advantage.

Peer triangulation uses Emmbi Industries, RDB Rasayans and Shree Tirupati Balajee Agro Trading, each imperfect. Emmbi provides a diversified packaging/qualification comparator but still had working-capital and pass-through constraints; its May 2025 CRISIL reaffirmation was withdrawn, not a live 2026 rating. RDB’s issuer-compiled FY26 revenue ₹ 117.75 crore/EBITDA₹ 21.53 crore shows different economics, with non-operating income affecting PAT, so its P/E cannot simply value Injecto. Balajee’s June 2026 rating letter records a downgrade to IVRBBB+/Stable on ₹ 104 crore facilities, showing sector expansion does not eliminate funding risk. No peer multiple is claimed as fair value.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Reported revenue is ₹ 96.2528 crore in FY23, ₹ 109.0479 crore in FY24, ₹ 261.4773 crore in FY25 and ₹ 375.5313 crore in FY26. Annual additions are ₹ 12.7951, ₹ 152.4294 and ₹ 114.0540 crore. The three-year reported CAGR is 57.43%; two-year FY24–26 CAGR 85.57%. The primary five-/ten-year comparable CAGR and comparable H 1 FY27 TTM are ND, not an annualized extrapolation from one partial period. Secondary rounded FY21/22 revenue 49/88 crore is retained only as background. [E02,E03]

FY26 manufactured sales rose 52.31%, traded sales 35.97%, total 43.62%; total volume sold increased 41.87% and blended revenue per tonne changed little. However, this mixed traded/manufactured unit is not a pure manufacturing utilization measure. Own-tape production fell 0.65% to 10,358 MT while external PP-fabric procurement rose 168%. The company attributes manufacturing revenue to the full-year leased plant, input-price pass-through and mix. PP fabric sales grew 62.83%, faster than bag sales 37.17%, so a generic claim that higher bag mix explains the entire increase is not borne out. [E04,E05]

CARE states the FY25 trading step-up included transfer of business from Hind Polyfabs. RHP says there were no material business additions/dispositions, while its own lease/perimeter facts show why constant-perimeter comparability still needs reconciliation. The evidence supports expansion in reported activity, not a precise organic five-year growth rate. REV is NS until the mix/transfer/price/volume bridge establishes a defensible scoring basis.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The existing FY26 detailed tape-capacity denominator is 10,870 MT, with output 10,358 MT and 95.29% utilization. Phase III proposes 2400 MT, with 1200 MT trial run on 1 July 2026 and the remainder not verified operating. Phase IV adds 4800 MT, with commercial start targeted April 2027 and total prospective capacity 18,070 MT. The latter is 66.2% above FY26, not a verified current output level. CTE does not substitute for CTO/factory approvals. [E15]

Phase IV detail totals ₹ 31.3774 crore excluding GST, financed by ₹ 30.5 crore IPO allocation and ₹.8774 crore identified internal component. Elsewhere a ₹ 31.3772 crore total differs by ₹.0002 crore, immaterial and preserved. The project still needs inventory/receivables, startup expense, taxes and possible overruns. At 4800 MT,75% utilization, ₹.015 crore/MT sales,15% EBITDA margin,20-year assumed depreciation and 40% sales working capital, modeled project revenue is ₹ 54 crore and post-tax incremental ROIC is only 7.47%, not a claimed actual return. The full utilization/realization matrix is embedded and compared with 13–17% WACC. [E17]

The five-year model separately forecasts manufacturing and trading revenue, margins, ONWC, capex, debt service, cash floors and dilution. Base terminal revenue ₹ 575 crore assumes manufacturing ₹ 335 crore plus trading ₹ 240 crore; new capacity alone does not prove that demand. CAP stays NS because actual cohort returns are not available and the short historical book return is contaminated by repricing/perimeter changes. CASH 2 imposes the explicit GQS cap 5; rapid reported growth does not qualify the business as a cash-generative compounder.

The disclosed ₹ 31.3774 crore budget is excluding GST and certain landed charges. The cash model adds a clearly assumed 5% landed/installation contingency (₹ 1.5689 crore) and 18% GST on the combined amount (₹ 5.9303 crore), for total Phase IV cash commitment of ₹ 38.8766 crore. The central model credits no GST recovery or tax-asset terminal value; a separate year-two recovery case is conditional on eligibility. This is a conservative cash buffer, not a legal tax determination. Other/maintenance capex is separately specified as all-in cash. The project return denominator includes this full commitment plus working capital; depreciation uses the ex-GST plant plus contingency.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters have extensive packaging experience and retain about 64.34% post-IPO according to September secondary ownership data; the primary post-listing shareholding/encumbrance annexure was not retrieved, so this is not asserted as a verified unpledged percentage. There is no OFS in the fresh IPO. ₹ 18 crore of old CCDs converted into 1.8 million shares in March 2025 at ₹ 100; this is not fresh FY25 cash simply because the cash-flow gross lines present equity issuance and debt decline. [E13,E14,E16]

The company acknowledges omitted RPT disclosures in FY23–25, says the transactions were already in revenue/expenses, has restated the schedules and retains auditor confirmation of ordinary-course, arm’s-length commercial terms. It applied for ROC adjudication on 20 August 2026 and said IPO/GCP funds would not pay resulting fines. Pending status is not a conviction or proof of diversion; correction is not final regulatory clearance. Several old filing delays are explained by consultants, procedural problems or Covid. Auditor resignation in June 2025 is attributed to other professional commitments, not a discovered scope dispute.

FY26 directors’ remuneration ₹ 1.02 crore was 17 times FY25 but 6.37% of PAT; scrutiny is proportionate, not an automatic abuse finding. Detailed RPT schedules report ₹ 13.9961 crore sales, ₹ 17.7242 crore purchases and ₹ 24.4938 crore other transactions. Related receivables require classification/recoverability explanation, and the group facility can create conflicts despite disclosed terms.

Promise/delivery chronology: June 2024 group-plant lease became operating production; July 2026 Phase III 1200 MT reached trial run, not demonstrated full commercial approvals; September 2026 IPO share issuance is corroborated; April 2027 Phase IV is a future target. Source strategy calling Phase III internally funded conflicts with the detailed SIDBI-funded objects narrative. No reported promise is silently upgraded to completed economics.

The RHP separately discloses a January 2026 GST notice against group company Hind Polyfabs and promoter Ramesh Kumar Rateria alleging invoices without actual goods movement and irregular input tax credit of ₹ 21.2735 crore. Hind had deposited ₹ 0.35 crore during investigation; its substantive reply was still being prepared, and the matter remained pending. Jupax faces a separate ₹ 5.3216 crore allegation and had deposited ₹ 0.30 crore; adjudication remained pending. These are allegations, not established findings. They are not automatically Injecto liabilities, and the Hind amount appearing under both promoter and group headings is not counted twice. Their relevance is heightened by the leased Hind plant, transferred trading activity and related receivables. A substantive rebuttal and final outcomes were not available at the cutoff. G1 is Hold, not Fail. [E22]

Injecto's own quantified GST orders total about ₹ 0.0145 crore; a further return-discrepancy notice contains uncertain liability, not an issued final demand. The issuer and two group companies also jointly seek recovery of ₹ 2.2365 crore principal, with ₹ 2.6144 crore including stated interest, from Janav entities. No issuer-only recoverable allocation is established, and no additional asset or cash is credited. Wider group tax disputes are not consolidated into Injecto's debt. [E22]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The three complete restated years and all calculation rows are embedded in the canonical record. FY24/FY25/FY26 revenue is 109.0479/261.4773/375.5313; operating EBITDA 12.3481/22.5686/38.0438; PAT 4.4436/8.1093/16.0128; CFO−12.9523/−16.8959/−48.8010 crore. Cumulative CFO/PAT uses the ratio of sums,−2.7533 x, not an average of yearly ratios. Reported FCF is−94.9210 crore after ₹ 16.2718 crore cash capex. Financing interest is outside CFO; after interest cumulative operating cash is−₹ 106.6106 crore. Removing restricted-deposit movements still leaves−₹ 73.7075 crore. [E02,E07,E08]

FY26 inventory grew 89.13% and AR 79.49%, faster than 43.62% sales growth. ₹ 66.0780 crore inventory absorption and ₹ 28.4605 crore AR absorption overwhelm ₹ 37.9581 crore pre-WC cash, even after ₹ 13.1529 crore supplier-credit support. The risk narrative reverses the payable sign, but the balance/cash tables reconcile: payable increases are cash sources. Capital expenditure is a separate investing use. Receivables older than six months rose from ₹.0979 crore to ₹ 7.2923 crore without a doubtful-debt provision; most remain recent and undisputed, but the ageing shift warrants collection evidence. [E08,E11]

Operating IC is ₹ 102.5327/143.9276/227.1735 crore and exactly reconciles to equity/debt after excluded restricted cash, income-tax assets, MAT credits, IPO prepayments and liabilities. Current reserves are not unrestricted cash:₹ 6.4814 crore of ₹ 6.5645 crore bank/cash is lien/margin money; available is ₹.0831 crore. Debt ₹ 165.1869 crore is 4.34 times EBITDA net of available cash, and EBIT/interest 2.88 x. Two-year incremental post-tax operating return 14.04% is a proxy, not a project IRR. Historical average and closing-capital definitions are separated. [E09,E17]

Other income is small in FY26 but FY24 includes ₹.5035 crore subsidy. MAT credit consumption and different tax rates explain why simplistic aggregator PAT₹ 17.47 crore conflicts with the RHP₹ 16.0128 crore; the later restated source governs. No extra tax asset is monetized. Prepaid IPO cost ₹.6229 crore offsets assumed remaining fees once; capital advances and CWIP are not counted twice. Small printed cash-flow rounding differences are kept as residuals, not exaggerated into a fraud claim. The material unresolved bridge is related receivables: generic AR note shows none from group while detailed RPT note identifies ₹ 4.0133 crore across Hind/Khatuwala. No extra asset is added.

The group GST allegations and joint recovery dispute reinforce the need to verify transaction substance and collectability without assuming the issuer itself owes every group claim. The detailed litigation notes supersede any generic impression that only minor filing lapses remain. [E22]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At the secondary ₹ 95.70 reference and 20,789,600 shares, market value is ₹ 198.96 crore. FY26 PAT on current shares gives EPS of ₹ 7.70 and P/E of 12.42×, not the pre-IPO EPS of ₹ 10.55. The deliberately stale March-balance EV/EBITDA cross-check is 9.57×. Current EV and P/B are ND because final IPO cash, uses and current net debt are unreconciled. [E16,E20]

Entry sources and uses reserve the entire ₹ 30.5 crore Phase IV allocation and assume ₹ 10 crore debt repayment. Total issue fees are assumed at ₹ 7.5 crore, less ₹ 0.6229 crore already prepaid. The bridge pays legacy net tax of ₹ 2.2506 crore, uses observed July secured debt and explicitly assumes unchanged March unsecured loans. Operating activity after March is modeled, not observed. The resulting ₹ 19.49 crore gap to required cash is conditional, not evidence of an actual October deficit. All ordinary and conditional non-rescue IRRs and entry prices remain null. [E18]

The separate rescue cases issue hypothetical equity at a 40% discount to the reference, charge 3% fees and retain operating cash at exit. Base gross proceeds of ₹ 20.0940 crore issue 3,499,481 new shares: share-count expansion is 16.83%, but existing-holder dilution is 14.41%. Rescue annualized returns are bear −40.64%, base 6.20% and bull 23.91%. None is an ordinary target. Base remains below the 15% hurdle even after financing and debt-rollover assumptions. Full annual rows, signed terminal cash, 12%/15%/18% hurdle entry values, margin-by-multiple sensitivity and capital, working-capital, rate and dilution stresses are included. [E19]

The reverse sensitivity tests a rescue-dependent revenue path. It does not reach the 15% hurdle anywhere within the checked bracket: the four-times-base boundary returns only about 10.21%. Required scale, terminal revenue and implied CAGR therefore remain null; no ordinary price-implied growth is asserted. A perpetual DCF is not used because segment capital and current funding are insufficiently established. Historical multiples and full incremental project capital provide cross-checks. Operational property is not added to enterprise value, and cash needed to run the business is not distributed twice. Execution costs are unverified; 1% and 3% cost sensitivities are not promised fills.

The dated ₹ 167 crore rated cash-credit limit less July working-capital debt of ₹ 112.9491 crore suggests a nominal ₹ 54.0509 crore difference, larger than the conditional entry gap. This is meaningful positive counterevidence. It is not established current drawable cash: expiry, drawing power, collateral eligibility and subsequent borrowing are unverified. Demand-loan call and partial bank non-renewal are modeled separately. G3 could be resolved by sufficiently complete published funding evidence; private daily bank statements are not required.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The thesis-break variable is whether incremental sales convert to collected cash after inventory and receivables, rather than merely whether the new tape line runs. A plausible linked failure is a large customer order reduction or polymer-price reversal → accumulated inventory and lower processing utilization → margin compression and slower collections → reduced drawing power → demand-loan/term repayment stress → emergency equity dilution and poor exit liquidity. Under the modeled bear, even hypothetical rescue financing leaves severe permanent per-share impairment. [E06–E11,E18,E19]

The strongest counterargument to a cautious view is tangible: a long operating history, near-full detailed utilization, real IPO equity, rising operating profit, lower largest-customer concentration and CARE’s adequate-liquidity opinion. These could support a successful expansion if inventory converts and bank headroom is genuinely drawable. The analysis does not claim today’s default or insolvency. It rejects the shortcut that these positives establish current financeability without reconciling earmarks, obligations and working capital.

Secured lenders and operational obligations have priority. Inventory at book cost is not an assured liquidation value; recoverable leased/owned assets and group receivables require separate evidence. A 20% inventory markdown alone is ₹ 28.04 crore,44.3% of March equity, before tax effects and without assuming all stock is impaired. A price decline alone would not resolve G2/G3/G4; clean funding and earnings-to-cash evidence would.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A tenfold share-price outcome requires annual growth of 58.49% over five years or 25.89% over ten years. Fivefold requires 37.97% over five years. These are mathematical requirements, not forecasts. Market value of ₹ 198.96 crore would need to reach about ₹ 1,989.56 crore for 10× at unchanged shares, and more after dilution. [E16,E19,E20]

The proposed 18,070 MT tape footprint is only 66.2% above FY26 capacity. Downstream processing and trading can expand beyond that physical denominator but require working capital and do not inherit manufacturing margins. A 10× case would need substantially wider customer access, sustained spreads, cash conversion, repeated financeable reinvestment and limited holder dilution, not merely Phase IV completion. With no verified incremental project return and persistent negative cash realization, classification is Speculative / unsupported. Upside is not impossible; a supported multibagger thesis is unavailable at this cutoff.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Post-IPO resources: obtain final prospectus, receipts, fees, the ₹ 30.5 crore Phase IV earmark, debt uses and general corporate purposes. Warning: unexplained recipient or object shifts. Thesis break: substantiated diversion or unfunded essential obligations. Review the next published proceeds/results filing.
2. Cash conversion: FY26 CFO was −₹ 48.80 crore and three-year CFO −₹ 78.65 crore. Warning: another profitable period with materially negative CFO. Improvement requires collections and inventory conversion without adverse new financing, not merely PAT growth.
3. Receivable ageing: balances older than six months rose to ₹ 7.2923 crore from ₹ 0.0979 crore. Warning: ageing outpaces collections or provisions lack support. Thesis break: irrecoverability materially impairs funding.
4. Inventory: ₹ 140.217 crore, up 89% in FY26. Separate raw materials, traded stock and finished goods. Warning: stock growth again exceeds sales while spreads fall. Thesis break: write-downs plus reduced drawing power cause a funding failure.
5. Phase III/IV: only 1,200 MT trial operation is evidenced for Phase III; Phase IV targets April 2027 at ₹ 31.3774 crore excluding GST. Verify CTO, factory approvals and commissioning. Economic success requires returns on full capex plus working capital above funding cost.
6. Governance and related parties: obtain outcomes of the ROC application and pending Hind/promoter and Jupax GST proceedings, including substantive replies. Reconcile the ₹ 4.0133 crore related receivable classification. A notice is not proof; an adverse established finding, material issuer exposure or minority harm could change G1 and GOV.
7. Organic economics: separate transferred trading activity, own manufacture, bought-in fabric processing, tonnage, realization and product margins. Require attributable NOPAT and full invested capital before scoring CAP.
8. Tradability: verify official history, current group/circuits, spreads and queues for the 1,200-share lot. Eighteen secondary observations and a last print of one lot do not establish an exit. This is a research plan, not an automated alert or trading instruction.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Research priorities are integrity/counterparty explanations, cash and funding, and attributable expansion economics. BQS, GQS and IAS are NS and excluded from numeric rankings. GOV 4 does not trigger Avoid — governance; pending serious allegations support G1 Hold but are not treated as proved misconduct. G3 is unresolved, not failed: no current default or demonstrated unfinanceable shortfall has been established. It nevertheless blocks ordinary return claims. Persistent CASH 2 caps GQS at 5 without creating a point from missing inputs. [E07–E22]

The compounder designation lacks both required factor evidence and resolved gates. No ordinary entry range is given, and the ₹ 5 lakh reference is not a personalized allocation. A lower price could improve hypothetical arithmetic but would not cure funding, reliability or tradability gaps. A reconciled post-IPO resources/obligations bridge, substantive litigation and counterparty explanations, documented approvals, comparable organic growth and attributable incremental returns would permit rescoring. Existing holders face a thesis-review and liquidity question; no trade instruction is invented without their holdings and constraints.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The principal original is the 7 September 2026 RHP, with a 24 August restated auditor report. CARE's 4 May 2026 rationale is a dated credit assessment. Exact security identity, lot and issued shares were checked against the 19 October official interoperable master. BSE listing details are corroborated through a mirror because the original exchange page returned HTTP 403. Screener and Equity Pandit provide secondary price/history context, not primary audit evidence. Peer numbers from the issuer comparison remain attributed. The June Balajee rating letter was read through primary PDF web access but no local original digest is claimed. [S1,S2,S3,S4,M1,M2,M3,P1,P2]

Analyst assumptions include 30% normalized tax, a 13–17% cost-of-capital range, a 15% equity hurdle, operating cash of 1% of sales, ₹ 7.5 crore issue fees, unchanged March unsecured loans in the July diagnostic, separate forecast manufacturing/trading economics, and hypothetical rescue terms. These are not management forecasts. Final IPO allocation, current resources/facilities, post-IPO pledges, original older accounts, counterparty classification, substantive GST responses and unit-level returns remain open.

Private analytical backups exclude original PDFs, raw HTML, OCR and images. They retain safe financial extracts, model code, citations and available source digests. Isolated reproduction proves calculation and artifact consistency, not external truth or fresh source authentication. The framework organizes judgment and is not a statistically validated return model. This is research, not personalized investment advice, guaranteed pricing or a trading instruction.
